small_guidance:
- Move the IC loop to the outermost position and the kd/kh/kw static loops inside; better, accumulate over IC as the innermost reduction using `tl.dot` by tiling IC as BLOCK_K (e.g. 16 or 32) so the per-iteration work becomes a small matmul instead of scalar outer products.
- Add a `triton.autotune` over `BLOCK_OC∈{32,64,128}`, `BLOCK_SP∈{32,64,128}`, `num_warps∈{4,8}`, `num_stages∈{2,3,4}`; current 32×64 with warps=4 is likely too small for a 64-OC, ~9.4k-spatial problem (16M output elements).
- Hoist `kd`/`kh`/`kw` divisibility checks: for `stride=2,pad=1`, only one of two `od+PAD-kd` values yields a valid `id`, so reorganize loops so half the kd/kh/kw combinations are skipped at compile time via a stride-aligned indexing scheme (gather only the valid parity).
large_guidance:
- Reformulate as an im2col-style GEMM with `tl.dot`: per program tile `(N, BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_SP)`, reduce over K = IC*KD*KH*KW with BLOCK_K=16/32. Weight is laid out as `[OC, IC*KD*KH*KW]` (precomputed once in `__init__` by permuting `[IC,OC,KD,KH,KW]→[OC,IC,KD,KH,KW]`), so the K-loop becomes a contiguous load + `tl.dot`, exploiting tensor cores.
- Exploit stride=2 sparsity: only kernel taps where `(od+PAD-kd)%2==0` contribute for a given output point. Precompute per-output-position which 8 of the 27 (kd,kh,kw) taps are live (2×2×2 pattern depending on parity of od,oh,ow), and process the 8 live taps × IC=32 = 256 K-elements per output — about 3× less work than iterating all 27.
- Fuse the entire epilogue `(2*y + ebias) * y + y` and use a channels-last (NDHWC) output write so the BLOCK_OC axis is contiguous in memory; this also lets the GEMM-K (IC) axis be contiguous on the input side if input is also converted to NDHWC once at entry.
